FIRST, THE SUPERSEDED RUN WAS NOT WASTED, AND I SAID EARLIER THAT IT WOULD BE. I would not have chosen to spend the box that way, but the result is better controlled than one run would have been.

SECOND, AND THIS IS THE PART THAT MATTERS. The 2168 vs 1209 headline is mostly queue wait -- your diagnostic sat behind your own superseded run -- so ignore it. The real comparison is phase wall time, and it decomposes cleanly:

  phase       the-charter   diagnostic
  artifacts     234.4 s       227.9 s
  outboard       96.8 s       218.0 s     <-- +121 s
  gate          732.8 s       732.9 s
  clients       138.3 s       137.7 s

Everything is flat except `outboard`, which your extra commit MORE THAN DOUBLES. That is the phase that runs `cargo test --manifest-path tools/digest/Cargo.toml`, and it is on BOTH the stage and merge phase lists -- so once this lands, every candidate from every campaign pays that +121 s, forever, on the one strictly serial box. At the current cadence that is real money in wall-clock terms and it is charged to people who are not you.

I am not asking you to drop it. I am asking you to know the number before you decide, and to consider whether the qualification work needs to run inside the gating phase at all, or whether it belongs behind an #[ignore] with its own entry point the way this repo handles other expensive probes. If it must be in `outboard`, that is a defensible call -- make it deliberately.

This also gives a measured edge to the flag I raised earlier: your suite spawns bounded contributor processes and does process-group signalling, in a phase that gates everyone. A doubling in that phase's wall time is the benign version of that risk; a leaked child or an escaped signal is the malign one, and it would present as an unattributable outboard timeout rather than as a digest bug. Bound the supervision with a timeout the test enforces, and kill children by process GROUP on every exit path including panic.

Nothing is blocking you. Both refs are green, main is unchanged at 3007f164c, and the queue is empty.
